The exact-head 202605 hardware validation requested in review is complete and is now recorded in the PR description.

On `testbed-bjw2-can-720dt-5` with `SONiC.20260510.12` (`644c1a022f`), the live detector probe confirmed `lspci` device `b274` resolves to `td3`. Pretest passed 11/3 expected skips. The initial Everflow target run plus five consecutive repeats each passed all four affected IPv4 M0 combinations: 24/24 affected cases, zero failures/errors.

Exact-head hardware evidence is now in the description: live 720DT PCI ID `b274` resolves to `td3`, pretest passed, and the initial target plus five consecutive internal-202605 runs passed 24/24 affected IPv4 cases. Exact-head CI and the post-undraft Copilot review are also clean.

This PR is ready for formal review and the 202605 backport decision.

**kvmtest-t2 failure analysis** — the red job is not caused by this change:

- The Elastictest plan for `impacted-area-kvmtest-t2` ran two scripts, `cacl/test_cacl_application.py` and `telemetry/test_telemetry.py`; it aborted because `telemetry/test_telemetry.py` had 2 failures ("stop whole test plan"). `gnmi/test_pygnmi_client.py` is correctly skipped on the t2 chassis by its conditional mark (`is_multi_asic` / `switch_type=='voq'`).
- This PR does not touch anything `tests/telemetry/test_telemetry.py` depends on (it imports only `gnmi_utils` and `telemetry_helper`; this PR changes `grpc_fixtures.py`, `pygnmi_client.py`, `test_pygnmi_client.py`, and gnmi-only conditional-mark entries). The telemetry suite landed in the plan only because a `tests/common/` change widens the t2 impacted area.
- `test_telemetry.py` is known not to support multi-ASIC T2: open issue #12083 (*"T2: Multi-asic support needed for telemetry/test_events, test_telemetry scripts"*, since 2024-03) — the tests don't use per-ASIC namespaces, which is exactly the VS t2 chassis in this job. No other recent 202605 (or master) PR has exercised this suite on kvmtest-t2, so there is no green baseline to point at; the failure is pre-existing branch behaviour rather than a regression.

I don't have permission to re-run the Azure pipeline on this repo (`/azp run` was rejected). @StormLiangMS / @hdwhdw — could one of you re-trigger it to confirm, or treat the t2 telemetry failure as the known #12083 issue? Hardware validation of this branch head on a 202605 image is 20/20 (see **Test result**).

> @Ryangwaite Thanks for fixing this. We encountered the same regression on a Mellanox-SN4700-O8V48 testbed: `hwsku.json` supplied the 200G platform default, while the connection graph specified 100G for twelve physical links. `deploy-mg` consequently restored 200G and left those ports oper-down.
> 
> The source tracking and precedence change in `minigraph_device.j2` look correct. However,  `ansible/templates/wan_minigraph_device.j2` still uses the old port_speed -> breakout_speed -> device_conn ordering.  `config_wan_sonic_testbed.yml` gathers the same port_alias and connection-graph facts and renders this WAN template, so JSON-backed WAN deployments appear to retain the same regression.
> 
> Could you apply the same port_speed_is_platform_default precedence logic to `wan_minigraph_device.j2` , or clarify why that rendering path is unaffected?
> 
> @r12f @Pterosaur for viz

I will but `ansible/templates/wan_minigraph_device.j2` doesn't exist publicly.

Good catch @ediwibowo-msft — you're right. The Debian ntpsec package ships with `restrict 127.0.0.1` and `restrict ::1` already in `/etc/ntpsec/ntp.conf`, so setup's `lineinfile` is a no-op there, but the teardown regex removal happily drops those preexisting lines.

Just pushed a follow-up commit that replaces the lineinfile-based teardown with a simple `cp`-to-backup at setup and `mv`-restore at teardown. Same idea for the whole config file (not just the restrict lines), which also lets us drop the pool/tos/server/refclock/interface cleanup regexes since the original file gets restored verbatim.

Diff summary: +13 / -20 in `ntp_helper.py`, no behavior change for the sync path. PTAL.
